questions.q: For ${Cr}_{2}{O}_{7}^{2 -} + 14H^{+} + 6e^{- yields} ⟶ 2{Cr}^{3 +} + 7{H}_{2}O, E^{0} = 1 . 33V$ at \left[{Cr}_{2}{O}_{7}^{2 -}\right] = 4 . 5$~millimole, \left[{Cr}^{3 +}\right] = 1 . 5$~millimole and $E = 1 . 067V$, then calculate the $pH$ of the solution.
questions.solution:
According to& the Nernst's equation:

$E = E^{°} - \dfrac{RT}{nF}lnQ$

So, by given value~of concentrations the above formula can be modified as

$E = E^{°} - \dfrac{0 . 059}{nF}log\dfrac{\left[{Cr}^{3 +}\right]2}{\left[{Cr}_{2}{O7}^{2 -}\right]\left[H^{+}\right]14}$

$1 . 067 = 1 . 33 - \dfrac{0 . 06}{6 \times 96500}log\dfrac{\left(15 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)2}{4 . 5 \times {10}^{- 3}\left[H^{+}\right]14}$

\left[H^{+}\right] = {10}^{- 2}M$

Hence, the concentration of~$H^{+}$~ion~will be

$pH = - log\left[H^{+}\right]pH = - log\left[{10}^{- 2}\right] = - ( - 2 ) \times \log_{10}\left(10\right)pH = 2$

$

It was found that when $2.1 \mathrm{~g}$ of $A$ was deposited, the weights of $B$ and $C$ deposited were $2.7 \mathrm{~g}$ and $9.6 \mathrm{~g}$. If the atomic mass of $A, B$ and $C$ respectively are 7,27 and 64 respectively, then the valancies of $A, B$ and $C$ respectively are
questions.solution: Using concept of Faraday law, Now, $A^{n_1^{+}}+n_1 e^{-} \longrightarrow A$ Similarly, $B^{n_2^{+}}+n_2 e^{-} \longrightarrow B$ and, $\mathrmC^{n_3^{+}}+n_3 e^{-} \longrightarrow C$ Since, charge is same then equivalent weight is same, $\begin{array}{ll} \therefore$& $\frac{2.1}{\frac{7}{n_1}}=\frac{2.7}{\frac{27}{n_2}}=\frac{7.2}{\frac{48}{n_3}}$\\ \therefore & $\frac{3 \times n_1}{10}=\frac{1 \times n_2}{10}=\frac{3 \times n_3}{2 \times 10} \therefore$n_1=$\frac{n_2}{3}=\frac{n_3}{2}$\\ \therefore & n_1=1, n_2=3 $\text { and }$n_3=2 \end{array} Hence, valencies of $A, B$ and $C$ are 1,3 and 2 .

questions.q: Find the emf of the following cell reaction, given ${E}_{{Cr}^{3 +} / {cr}^{2 +}}^{0} = - 0 . 72V$ and ${E}_{{Fe}^{2 +} / Fe} = 0- 0 . 42V$ at $25 ° C$ is $Cr\left|{Cr}^{3 +} ( 0 . 1M ) ‖ {Fe}^{2 +} ( 0 . 1M )\right|Fe$
questions.solution:
The given cell is:

$Cr\left|{Cr}^{3 +} ( 0 . 1M ) ‖ {Fe}^{2 +} ( 0 . 1M )\right|Fe$

The half reactions can be written~as:

$Cr \to {Cr}^{3 +} + 3e^{- 1}E^{°} = - 0 . 72V{Fe}^{2 +} + 2e^{- 1} \to FeE^{°} = - 0 . 42V$

The full reaction of the operating cell is:

$3{Fe}^{2 +} + 2Cr \to 2{Cr}^{3 +} + 3Fe$

Now, emf of the cell reaction is~

$E^{°}cell = E^{°}cathode - E^{°}anodeE^{°}cell = - 0 . 42 - ( - 0 . 72 ) = 0 . 30V$

Therefore,

${E}_{cell} = E^{°}cell - \dfrac{nRT}{F}lnQ$

${E}_{cell} = E^{°}cell - \dfrac{2 . 303nRT}{F}\log_{10}\dfrac{\left[{Cr}^{3 +}\right]2}{\left[{Fe}^{2 +}\right]3}{E}_{cell} = 0 . 3 - \dfrac{0 . 059}{6}\log_{10}\dfrac{\left[0 . 1\right]2}{\left[0 . 1\right]3}{E}_{cell} \approx 0 . 30V$

questions.q: At $291K$, saturated solution of ${BaSO}_{4}$ was found to have a specific conductivity of $3 . 648 \times {10}^{- 6}{ohm}^{- 1}{cm}^{- 1}$ and that of water being used is $1 . 25 \times {10}^{- 6}{ohm}^{- 1}{cm}^{- 1}$. If the ionic conductance's of ${Ba}^{2 +}$ and ${SO}_{4}^{2 -}$ are $110$ and $136 . 6{ohm}^{- 1}{cm}^{2}{mol}^{- 1}$ respectively, the solubility of ${BaSO}_{4}$ at $291K$ will be [Atomic masses of  \leftBa - 137, S - 32, 0 - 16\right]$
questions.solution:
According to Kohlrausch's law

${λ}^{°}m\left({BaSO}_{4}\right) = {λ}^{°}m\left({Ba}^{2 +}\right) + {λ}^{°}m\left({SO4}^{2 -}\right){λ}^{°}m\left({BaSO}_{4}\right) = 110 + 136 . 6{λ}^{°}m\left({BaSO}_{4}\right) = 246 . 6{ohm}^{- 1}{cm}^{- 1}$

Now,~the solubility product of~${BaSO}_{4}$~can be determined by:

${K}_{BaSO4} = {K}_{BaSO4}\left(solution\right) - {K}_{water}{K}_{BaSO4} = 3 . 648 \times {10}^{- 6} - 1 . 25 \times {10}^{- 6}{K}_{BaSO4} = 2 . 398 \times {10}^{- 6}S{cm}^{- 1}$

Finally, the molar conductivity will be:

${λ}^{°}m = \dfrac{K \times 100}{Solubility}{λ}^{°}m = \dfrac{2 . 398 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 100}{246 . 6}{λ}^{°}m = 9 . 72 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 233{λ}^{°}m = 2 . 26 \times {10}^{- 3}\dfrac{g}{L}$

questions.q: Salts of $A$ (atomic weight $8$), $B$ (atomic weight $18$) and $C$ (atomic weight $50$) were electrolysed under identical conditions using the same quantity of electricity. It was found that $2 . 4g$ of $A$ was deposited, the weight of $B$ and $C$ deposited are $1 . 8g$ and $7 . 5g$ respectively. The valences of $A, B$ and $C$ are, respectively,
questions.solution:
According to the Faraday's law of electrolysis,

$W = ZQ = \dfrac{E}{96500}Q$

For the compound $A$,~

Equivalent mass of $A$ =~$\dfrac{Atomicmass}{Valency} = \dfrac{8}{x}$

$x$~is the valency factor for compound $A$.

So,~$W = \dfrac{E}{96500}Q = \dfrac{\dfrac{8}{x}}{96500}Qx = \dfrac{7}{2 . 4 \times 96500}Q$

For compound $B$,

Equivalent mass of $B$=$\dfrac{Atomicmass}{Valency} = \dfrac{18}{y}$

$y$~is the valency factor for compound $B$.

So,~$W = \dfrac{E}{96500}Q = \dfrac{\dfrac{18}{y}}{96500}Qy = \dfrac{27}{1 . 8 \times 96500}Q$

For compound $C$,

Equivalent mass of $C$ =~$\dfrac{Atomicmass}{Valency} = \dfrac{50}{z}$

$z$~is the valency factor for compound $C$.

So,~$W = \dfrac{E}{96500}Q = \dfrac{\dfrac{50}{z}}{96500}Qz = \dfrac{50}{7 . 5 \times 96500}Q$

Hence,~$x: y: z = \dfrac{8}{2 . 4}: \dfrac{18}{1 . 8}: \dfrac{50}{7 . 5} = 3 . 33: 10: 6 . 66x: y: z = 1: 3: 2$

Hence,~the valencies of $A, B$ and $C$ respectively are~$1, 3, 2$.
questions.source: 99 Percentile Qs Bank for JEE Main

questions.solution:
$Cu^{+} + e^{-} \to Cu; E ° = 0.52$ V

$\Delta{G}_{1} = - nFE ° = - 1 \times 96500 \times 0.52$ ...(i)

or $Cu^{+} \to Cu^{2 +} + e^{-}; E ° = - 0.16$ V

$= - \left($96500 \times0.36\right)$

$\text{=} - \text{34740 J}\text{=} - \text{34}\text{.740}\text{kJ}$

questions.q: If ' $A$ ' is the reactant and ' $P$ ' is the product, which one of the following is the correct form of Nernst equation?
questions.solution: According to Nernst equation : $\begin{aligned} & E=E^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}-\frac{R T}{n F} \ln \frac{[\text { Product }]}{[\text { Reactant }]} \\ & \text { or, } \quad E=E^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}-\frac{R T}{n F} \ln \frac{[P]}{[A]} \\ & \text { or, } \quad E-E^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}=-\frac{R T}{n F} \ln \left[\frac{P}{A}\right] \\ & \text { or, } \quad\left[\frac{A}{P}\right]=e^{\left[\frac{n F}{R T}\left(E-E^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}\right)\right]} \\ & \text { or } \quad \frac{[A]}{[P]}=\exp ^{\left[\frac{n F}{R T}\left(E-E^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}\right)\right]} \\ & \end{aligned}$ Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.
